## Compute Dispersion


## import dataset with all gradients

```{r}
combined_gradients <- pc_read_gradients(c("rs2", "rs3"), data_root = paths$data_root) %>%
  select(NECOS_ID, scan, parcel, V1, V2, V3)

# Load and process IV dataframe
IV <- pc_mean_fd(paths$data_root, scans = c("rest2", "rest3")) %>%
  select(NECOS_ID, scan, headmotion, stress = Group)

parcel_labels <- pc_parcel_labels(paths$data_root) %>%
  select(X7networks_order,X7networks)%>%
  rename(parcel = X7networks_order)


# Merging the gradients data with IV
final_data <- merge(IV, combined_gradients, by = c("NECOS_ID", "scan"))
final_data <- merge(parcel_labels[c("parcel", "X7networks")], final_data, by = c("parcel"))

pc_write_csv(final_data, file.path(tables_dir, "dispersion_within_gradients_parcel_labels_iv.csv"))

```

## create the centroid dataset

calculate the centroid of the network as the mean of all parcels in the 3D space
```{r}
# Next we calculate the centroid for each network based on its corresponding parcels

library(dplyr)

mean_centroids <- final_data %>%
  group_by(NECOS_ID, X7networks, scan) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_V1 = mean(V1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_V2 = mean(V2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_V3 = mean(V3, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pc_write_csv(mean_centroids, file.path(tables_dir, "dispersion_within_mean_centroids.csv"))


```

## Compute the within network dispersion
```{r}

# Function to calculate Euclidean distance in 3D for each parcel
calculate_distance_for_parcel <- function(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2) {
  sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 + (z2 - z1)^2)
}

# Calculate distances for each parcel using mean centroids
final_data_with_distance <- final_data %>%
  left_join(mean_centroids, by = c("NECOS_ID", "X7networks", "scan")) %>%
  mutate(distance_to_mean_centroid = calculate_distance_for_parcel(V1, V2, V3, mean_V1, mean_V2, mean_V3))

# Average distances for each NECOS_ID, network, and scan using mean centroids
within_dispersion <- final_data_with_distance %>%
  group_by(NECOS_ID, X7networks, scan) %>%
  mutate(X7networks = ifelse(X7networks %in% c("Salience / Ventral Attn"), "Salience", X7networks))%>%
  summarise(within_dispersion = mean(distance_to_mean_centroid, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')


# Load and process IV dataframe
IV <- pc_mean_fd(paths$data_root, scans = c("rest2", "rest3")) %>%
  select(NECOS_ID, scan, headmotion, stress = Group)


# Merging the gradients data with IV
within_dispersion <- merge(IV, within_dispersion, by = c("NECOS_ID", "scan"))

# Save the results for mean centroids
pc_write_csv(within_dispersion, file.path(tables_dir, "dispersion_mean_within_networks.csv"))

```

### 1. Normality assumption of the dependent variable

**a. histogram**

```{r}
# Function to create and save histogram for mean distances by network
create_save_histogram_mean_by_network <- function(data, distance_column, title_prefix, file_prefix, scan, network) {
  # Check if the distance_column is present in the data
  if (!distance_column %in% colnames(data)) {
    stop(paste("Error: Column", distance_column, "not found in the data."))
  }

  # Create histogram plot
  p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = distance_column)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", color = "black") +
    ggtitle(paste(title_prefix, " - ", distance_column, " - Scan: ", scan, " - Network: ", network)) +
    xlab("Distance") +
    ylab("Frequency")

  # Construct file path
  file_path <- file.path(diag_hist_dir, paste0("dispersion_within_histogram_", scan, "_", network, ".svg"))

  # Save the plot
  ggsave(filename = file_path, plot = p, width = 10, height = 8, device = "svg")
}

# Distance type to plot
distance_type <- "within_dispersion"

# Assuming the networks are named as 'Default', 'Control', and 'Salience'
networks <- c("Default", "Control", "Salience")


# Create and save histograms for mean distances for each scan and network
for (scan in unique(within_dispersion$scan)) {
  for (network in networks) {
    subset_data <- within_dispersion[within_dispersion$scan == scan & within_dispersion$X7networks == network, ]
    create_save_histogram_mean_by_network(subset_data, distance_type, "Mean Distances", "mean_distances", scan, network)
  }
}


```

**b. qq-plots**

```{r}
# Function to create and save QQ plot for mean distances by network
create_save_qqplot_mean_by_network <- function(data, distance_column, title_prefix, file_prefix, scan, network) {
  # Check if the distance_column is present in the data
  if (!distance_column %in% colnames(data)) {
    stop(paste("Error: Column", distance_column, "not found in the data."))
  }

  # Create QQ plot
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(sample = !!sym(distance_column))) +
    stat_qq() +
    stat_qq_line() +
    ggtitle(paste(title_prefix, " - ", distance_column, " - Scan: ", scan, " - Network: ", network)) +
    xlab("Theoretical Quantiles") +
    ylab("Sample Quantiles")

  # Construct file path
  file_path <- file.path(diag_qq_dir, paste0("dispersion_within_qq_", scan, "_", network, ".svg"))

  # Save the plot as SVG
  ggsave(filename = file_path, plot = p, width = 10, height = 8, device = "svg")
}

# Distance type to plot
distance_type <- "within_dispersion"

# Create and save QQ plots for mean distances for each scan and network
for (scan in unique(within_dispersion$scan)) {
  for (network in networks) {
    subset_data <- within_dispersion[within_dispersion$scan == scan & within_dispersion$X7networks == network, ]
    create_save_qqplot_mean_by_network(subset_data, distance_type, "Mean Distances QQ Plot", "mean_distances_qq", scan, network)
  }
}

```

### 2. Define model

Define 3 models of the same type with different dependent variables (between distance of centroids)
## between network dispersion
```{r}

# Function to run the model using afex::mixed
run_model <- function(network) {
  
   # Splitting the dataframe by '7networks'
  split_data <- split(within_dispersion, within_dispersion$`X7networks`)
  
  # Construct the formula
  model_formula <- as.formula("within_dispersion ~ stress * scan + headmotion + (1 | NECOS_ID)")

  # Extract the dataframe associated with the specified network
  df <- split_data[[network]]

  # Fit the mixed model using afex::mixed
  afex_model <- mixed(model_formula, data = df)
  
  return(afex_model)
}


# Function to run the model using lme4::lmer
lmer_run_model <- function(network) {
 # Splitting the dataframe by '7networks'
  split_data <- split(within_dispersion, within_dispersion$`X7networks`)
  
  # Construct the formula
  model_formula <- as.formula("within_dispersion ~ stress * scan + headmotion + (1 | NECOS_ID)")

  # Extract the dataframe associated with the specified network
  df <- split_data[[network]]
  
  # Fit the mixed model using afex::mixed
  lmer_model <- lme4::lmer(model_formula, data = df)
  

  return(lmer_model)
}


# Run afex models for each distance measure
afex_model_control <- run_model("Control")
afex_model_default <- run_model("Default")
afex_model_salience <- run_model("Salience")

# run lmer models for each distance measure to compute plots easier later on
lmer_model_control <- lmer_run_model("Control")
lmer_model_default <- lmer_run_model("Default")
lmer_model_salience <- lmer_run_model("Salience")

# extract p-values of afex models
default_control <- afex_model_control$anova_table$`Pr(>F)`
control_p <- default_control[4]

default_salience <- afex_model_default$anova_table$`Pr(>F)`
default_p <- default_salience[4]

control_salience <- afex_model_salience$anova_table$`Pr(>F)`
salience_p <- control_salience[4]

# Extract p-values
p_values_interaction <- c(
  control_p,
  default_p,
  salience_p
)

# Apply Bonferroni correction across all three p-values
adjusted_p_values <- p.adjust(p_values_interaction, method = "bonferroni")

# Create a data frame with results
p_value_df <- data.frame(
  Distance_Type = c("Control", "Default", "Salience"),
  P_Value = p_values_interaction,
  Adjusted_P_Value = adjusted_p_values
)
#save df
pc_write_csv(p_value_df, file.path(models_dir, "dispersion_within_network_pvalues.csv"))


# Function to extract relevant summary data from lmer models
extract_lmer_summary <- function(model) {
  summary_model <- summary(model)
  fixed_effects <- summary_model$coefficients
  random_effects_var <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model))
  
  return(list(fixed_effects = fixed_effects, random_effects_var = random_effects_var))
}

# Extract summary data from each lmer model
summary_control <- extract_lmer_summary(lmer_model_control)
summary_default <- extract_lmer_summary(lmer_model_default)
summary_salience <- extract_lmer_summary(lmer_model_salience)

# Extract fixed effects data into separate data frames
fe_control_df <- as.data.frame(summary_control$fixed_effects)
fe_control_df$Model <- "Control"

fe_default_df <- as.data.frame(summary_default$fixed_effects)
fe_default_df$Model <- "Default"

fe_salience_df <- as.data.frame(summary_salience$fixed_effects)
fe_salience_df$Model <- "Salience"

# Combine the fixed effects data frames
combined_fe_df <- rbind(fe_control_df, fe_default_df, fe_salience_df)

# Add P_Value and Adjusted_P_Value columns
combined_fe_df$P_Value_Scan_Stress <- rep(p_values_interaction, each = nrow(combined_fe_df) / 3)
combined_fe_df$Adjusted_P_Value_Scan_Stress <- rep(adjusted_p_values, each = nrow(combined_fe_df) / 3)

# Save the combined data frame
pc_write_csv(combined_fe_df, file.path(models_dir, "dispersion_within_network_model_results.csv"))

```

### 3. Check model assumptions

**a. normality of residuals**

```{r}
all_lmer_models <- list(
  Control = lmer_model_control,
  Default = lmer_model_default,
  Salience = lmer_model_salience
)

create_save_qqplot_residuals <- function(lmer_model, network, file_prefix) {
  res_df <- data.frame(residuals = residuals(lmer_model))

  p <- ggplot(res_df, aes(sample = residuals)) +
    stat_qq() +
    stat_qq_line() +
    ggtitle(paste("Residuals QQ Plot - Network:", network)) +
    xlab("Theoretical Quantiles") +
    ylab("Sample Quantiles")

  file_path <- file.path(diag_qq_dir, paste0(file_prefix, "_", network, ".svg"))
  ggsave(filename = file_path, plot = p, width = 10, height = 8, device = "svg")
}

purrr::walk(names(all_lmer_models), function(network) {
  create_save_qqplot_residuals(all_lmer_models[[network]], network, "dispersion_within_residuals_qq")
})
```

**b. homoscedasticity**

```{r}
create_save_homoscedasticity_plot <- function(lmer_model, network, file_prefix) {
  df <- data.frame(
    Fitted = predict(lmer_model),
    Residuals = resid(lmer_model)
  )

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Fitted, y = Residuals)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    ggtitle(paste("Homoscedasticity Plot - Network:", network)) +
    xlab("Fitted Values") +
    ylab("Residuals")

  file_path <- file.path(diag_resid_dir, paste0(file_prefix, "_", network, ".svg"))
  ggsave(filename = file_path, plot = p, width = 10, height = 8, device = "svg")
}

purrr::walk(names(all_lmer_models), function(network) {
  create_save_homoscedasticity_plot(all_lmer_models[[network]], network, "dispersion_within_homoscedasticity")
})
```

**c. independence (auto-correlation of the residuals)**

```{r}
durbin_watson_df <- data.frame(
  Model = names(all_lmer_models),
  Durbin_Watson_Statistic = purrr::map_dbl(all_lmer_models, ~ as.numeric(car::durbinWatsonTest(residuals(.x))))
)

pc_write_csv(durbin_watson_df, file.path(diagnostics_dir, "dispersion_within_network_durbin_watson.csv"))
```

**d. multi-collinearity: Variance Inflation Factor (VIF)**

```{r}
multicollinearity <- purrr::map(all_lmer_models, vif)
terms <- names(multicollinearity[[1]])
vif_df <- data.frame(Term = terms)

for (model_name in names(multicollinearity)) {
  vif_df[[model_name]] <- multicollinearity[[model_name]]
}

pc_write_csv(vif_df, file.path(diagnostics_dir, "dispersion_within_network_vif.csv"))
```
